meaning: The trained model that maps what the robot senses to what it does next, run on the robot's clock.
The input to a policy at one instant: on the SO-101, six joint angles and one image per camera.
The output of a policy at one instant: on the SO-101, six target joint angles.
One recorded attempt at the task: a table with one row of observation and action per tick, plus the camera video.
A collection of episodes that a policy is trained on.
The open-source robot-learning library this dive follows for recording, training and running policies on the SO-101.
The part of a GPU that does the matrix arithmetic of training and inference.
The part of a GPU that draws images by tracing light, used to render what a simulated camera sees.
The parts of a GPU that compress and decompress video.
A model that predicts what happens next if the robot takes a given action.
A family of world models that predicts in a compact internal representation of the scene.
A policy built on a network that takes camera images and a text instruction.
Training in which a model improves by trial and reward.
The set of counters built into a processor that show where its time goes.
The AWS network fabric for multi-node training jobs, covered in its own dive.
